topic: The day that never ends in Svalbard
angle: In Svalbard the sun doesn't set for four months, and Earth's tilt is the bug
title: This Town Has No Night for 4 Months
description: Earth's 23.4° tilt breaks the day-night cycle near the poles.

scenes.narration: Earth has a bug: in one town, the sun just won't set.
Welcome to Longyearbyen, Svalbard, one of the northernmost towns on the planet.
From April to August, daylight lasts around the clock. That's roughly one hundred and twenty days without a sunset.
The cause is Earth's tilt. Our planet leans about twenty three degrees on its axis.
In summer the North Pole leans toward the sun, so the far north keeps spinning in daylight.
Then it flips. Winter brings the polar night, months when the sun never rises at all.
Locals sleep with blackout curtains in summer, and the town throws a festival when the sun returns.
So it's not a glitch after all. It's a feature of a tilted planet. Follow for more of Earth's bugs.
